rationale_bullets: Proven option engine returns: Hellums 2025 - 304 carries (2nd nationally), 1,223 yds, 18 rush TD (T-3rd), PFF 77.0 (AAC +0.4 -> 77.4 adj = 61st pctile as-played) after starting the year 3rd string (Athlon 2026).
Continuity is the whole case: same scheme (Monken yr 13), second full offseason as QB1, spring reports specific improvement in 'footwork, fundamentals, and reads' (GBK 2026-04-20).
The cap is the passing: 694 yds at 54% (4-3) in 2025 - defenses can load the box; the unit's national ceiling is bounded by design.
62 = above-average FBS QB unit: a returning percentile-61 producer with system fit, graded slightly above his as-played level for the experience trajectory, held below 70 by the one-dimensionality.

rationale_bullets: 2025 corps as-played was 26th pctile and lost its best piece: Short (78.6 PFF; 1,009 scrimmage yds) departed, Bartosh stepped away with a neck injury ('hurting Army's big-play ability' - Athlon 2026).

The emergence is real but small-sample: Nwawuihe - 'Army found its featured back' (Athlon) - 196 yds at 9.3/carry incl. 171 + 2 TD in the Fenway Bowl (vs a depleted UConn per PS - discounted accordingly); QB background adds formation value.

Returning role players are adequate: Howard (13 starts at slotback), Rendina (72.2/39), C.Smith (67.0/56); and Athlon notes the staff wants Hellums (40% of carries) 'to share the touches' - more volume coming to this group.
38 = below-average nationally: one promising sophomore + committee depth in a scheme that manufactures RB efficiency, minus the two biggest 2025 playmakers.

All three contributors return (PS: 'more experienced'): Anderson - PFF 78.1, 381 yds at 27.2/catch (9 starts) - a legitimate deep threat who converts the offense's rare shots; TE Poloskey (64.6/105, 13 starts); Olawole depth.

rationale_bullets: 2025 as-played was 94th pctile nationally (80.7 adj on 4,475 snaps) and FOUR of five starters return (Athlon): C Small (79.6/893; 39 consecutive starts; 1st-tm All-AAC - PS), RT Williams (90.3/892), LT Appleton (72.2/892), RG Gennarelli (62.8/674).
The one loss is the best grade: Jeffcoat (91.3/890); Kloska (6 gm 2025) steps in at LG. Small (spring, attributed): the 2026 group 'could match the caliber of Army's 2024 line' (GBK 2026-04-20).

Honesty about shape: this is run-block excellence (team RBLK 86.4) with poor pass pro (PBLK 56.6) that the scheme rarely exposes - the grade prices what the unit does at elite level, discounted for what it can't.
84 = at the Texas Tech OL anchor with a better sketch (3 returners at 72+ raw incl. a 90.3, vs the anchor's 0 at 72+), below Kentucky-DL-91 for the Jeffcoat loss + one-dimensionality.

grades_detail.g5_guard_note: G5 >75 justified: 94th-pctile 2025 as-played on 4,475 snaps; 4/5 starters return incl. 90.3-graded RT and All-AAC C with 39 straight starts; two magazines + spring reporting corroborate the unit as the team's identity.

rationale_bullets: The tension is real and both halves are true: Athlon calls DL 'Army's most experienced defensive unit' (all three starters return - Bousum 66.6/631 w/ 29 tkl 8 TFL and 'pro potential', Harris-Miller 66.5/309 3rd-yr starter, Stowers 61.1/225), yet the unit's 2025 as-played national percentile was 9 after the AAC DL adjustment (-5.9).
Returning-weighted baseline: ~65.5 raw -> ~59.6 adj ≈ p22 nationally - the returners are experienced but graded modestly, and ~45% of unit snaps left (Ford 64.8/670, Latore 64.3/491, Tuioti).

Option-defense context (fewer snaps behind a clock-eating offense; bend-don't-break) explains some team-level success (PA 21.6/gm) that unit grades don't credit - noted, worth a small nudge, not a regrade.

25 = bottom-third-to-quartile: continuity + Bousum's trajectory hold it above the FIU-QB-15 anchor; the national quality evidence keeps it well under Illinois-RB-32... at 25, matching the WKU-OL sketch level.

rationale_bullets: Worst-case configuration: the 2025 unit was 2nd-pctile nationally as-played (44.7 adj - the AAC LB offset of -10.7 is brutal and the LB caution rule applies to both directions), and BOTH 802-snap starters (captains Fortner 55.8, Thomas 55.1) are gone.

The replacements have essentially no production: Banks (8 gm, 2 tkl - 'first shot'), Moss (4 gm), Walton (11 gm, 8 tkl); Athlon: the job 'may not be decided until fall camp' and 'the inexperience at inside linebacker is also concerning'; Monken himself expects early mental errors (GBK 2026-04-20).

Mitigants are thin but real: internal DC promotion (Dixon) preserves scheme; academy LBs are systematically developed; and the LB noise rule means the 2nd-pctile baseline overstates certainty of badness.
15 = above the FAU-DB-6 anchor (which was a *functioning* poor unit at volume), below WKU-OL-25: an unproven room inheriting the weakest-graded context in the league.
Four of five secondary starters gone (Larkin 72.3/724, Matteson 68.5/679, Shields 62.7/675, Weaver 67.0/477, plus Nnadozie 79.7/248) from a unit that was only 32nd pctile as-played.

The one returner is genuinely useful: CB Mayes (65.5/692) produced 4 INT + 3 PBU in 2025 - ballhawk output - but Athlon frames it exactly: 'Army's lone returning starter in the secondary needs to have a big season.'
Everything else is projection: Porter (SO, 11 gm, 2 tkl) at CB2, C.Williams (72.0 on 32 snaps - a hint) at safety, rover Tallman (2 tkl); 'younger on defense than in years past' (Athlon 2026).
22 = bottom-sixth nationally: one proven piece + youth, slightly better than the LB room because Mayes is real and the baseline was less dire.
data_gaps: Both safety spots + rover effectively unproven (32 combined meaningful snaps)

rationale_bullets: Both specialists return with documented quality: K Jones - 15 FG in 2025 (most by an Army kicker since 2010), made his final 5 attempts including a walk-off winner vs Air Force; P Wagenseller - 43.1 avg, 'a field-position game-changer' (Athlon 2026); both drew specific Monken praise in spring (GBK 2026-04-20).
2025 team SPEC was 75.3 (PFF) - solidly above average - and unlike Iowa/Memphis, the people who earned it are back.
Academy coverage-unit culture (deep, disciplined rosters) is a stable prior; the open item is the return game (Short handled touches; 2026 roles unnamed - logged gap).
65 = comfortably above average: returning proven K + P + system, held under 70 by the unnamed returners.
